tips: Load your Suica/Pasmo into Apple Wallet before landing to breeze through the Haneda gates.
Hit the ATM at Haneda; with USD/JPY at ~161, your dollars stretch far for cash-first spots like Omoide Yokocho.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: December evenings in Tokyo are cold and dry, but occasional rain is possible. The Shibuya Blue Cave illumination is an outdoor walk—dress warmly and carry a compact umbrella.
tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast; if you haven't pre-booked, pivot to the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building view on Dec 15th or Mag's Park.
Harajuku's Takeshita Street is notoriously crowded on weekend afternoons—stick to the Cat Street vintage crawl for a breather.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the outdoor Nakamise snack gauntlet and Ueno Ameyoko market stalls.

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Tokyo National Museum (samurai swords + armor, 2h) slots between Asakusa and Akiba on the same line.

teamLab Planets requires walking barefoot in water; wear easy-slip shoes and roll up your pants.
Depachika (basement food halls) close around 19:00-20:00; do your grazing raid at 15:00, not after dinner.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: High rain risk for this coastal day trip. The Enoshima tram ride and Fuji-over-Sagami-Bay sunset are completely weather-dependent.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle

Start the Airbnb laundry NOW before the farewell dinner so you have clean clothes for Kyoto tomorrow.
For the Nozomi shinkansen, reserve seats A and B (left side) for the best chance at the Mt. Fuji view around minute 40.
Nishiki Market stalls start closing around 17:00; do your grazing run early upon arrival.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Cold, crisp December mornings are perfect for Fushimi Inari, but the exposed summit can be freezing. Rain makes the stone paths extremely slippery.

Funaoka Onsen is a classic sento but has tattoo restrictions; check ahead or cover small tattoos if needed.

Uji matcha is potent; Byodo-in and the river walk are a serene, uncrowded contrast to the Nintendo Museum hype.

Use single-rider lines for Harry Potter and Jurassic World to save time if the group is willing to split up briefly.

Do a tax-free paperwork check tonight: ensure all receipts are stapled in your passports and purchases are accessible for customs.
For the shinkansen back to Tokyo, reserve seats A and B (left side) again for one last Mt. Fuji view.
Zero out your Suica cards at the konbini or use them for final gachapon—refunds aren't available at the airport.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~161, your dollars go far—withdraw large sums from 7-Eleven ATMs to avoid per-transaction fees, and pay cash at smaller temples, markets, and street stalls.
December days are short; sunset is around 16:30. Plan outdoor sightseeing and illumination walks early, as it gets dark and cold quickly.
Always carry a compact umbrella and dress in layers. The weather is mostly dry, but a cold rain can ruin outdoor-heavy days like Kamakura or Arashiyama if you aren't prepared.
